findings.summary: The begin path has no test of the pass after a failure write that did not land, where a session may already be running
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance. The three injected-boundary tests and the restart test all go through the ready-timeout path in _awaitLaunch. On the begin path the only test ("a launch that can neither begin nor end...") stops at the launches still being 'queued'; it never runs the next pass. That is the one place where a rolled-back failure write is followed by a second run of _beginLaunch with a session the first run started still live. By reading, the next pass finds it through store.sessions.getActive and waits on it without calling launchSession again, but nothing holds that: a change that launched a second session for the same consent on that path would pass the suite. Add a next-pass assertion to that test: restore the store, tick again, and assert launchSession was called once in total for that launch, the launch waits on the session already started, and no failure notice exists.

findings.summary: A failure write that throws once for a launch past its wait is rewritten in the same pass as launch-error
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance. In _advanceLaunches (lib/bridge-gateway.js, the catch around _awaitLaunch), a throw from _launchFailed(flying, 'ready-timeout') or any other code is caught and, once the wait is over, answered at once with _launchFailed(flying, 'launch-error'). When the first throw was transient, the second lands: the launch, the route and the operator's notice all say launch-error for what was a ready-timeout or identity-changed. Before this change that happened only when the first of the three writes threw; now a throw anywhere in the one write leads to it. The new tests do not see it because their injection lasts the whole pass. The operator is still told once and the state is consistent, so this is a wrong closed code in a rare case, not a lost notice. If it is worth closing: keep the catch for failures of the judging only, and let a failed failure-write wait for the next pass, which re-derives the true code.

observations.summary: A thrown null, undefined or frozen value loses the failureNotWritten mark
observations.recommendation: Scope: instance. In _launchFailed (lib/bridge-gateway.js:958) Object.assign(err, {failureNotWritten: true}) works for an Error and for a thrown string or number (it is boxed and the boxed value is thrown, mark intact). For a thrown null or undefined, or a frozen object, Object.assign itself throws a TypeError that carries no mark, so the caller falls back to what it did before this delta: it ends the launch as launch-error in the same pass. Nothing in the store or node:sqlite throws such a value, and the fallback is the old behaviour, not a wedge or a lost notice. ACCEPT is the default; fixing it moves the tree and costs a round.
